limits: Compile-time counts only: a lost loop is only potentially expensive. How often it runs (its hotness) is unknown at compile time, so no runtime cost is claimed from this census.
Every vectorized loop counts once per function it was compiled into: a header loop inlined into three functions counts three times. Unique source locations are reported beside the counts.
One toolchain and target: clang 18 with libc++ 18 (Ubuntu noble), -O2, baseline x86-64 (SSE2), FAST mode only. Other compilers, -march levels and the extensive mode are not covered.
Header-only libraries are measured through a small driver that instantiates common operations; loops the driver does not instantiate are not counted.
The classification of why a loop lost SIMD is a regular-expression heuristic over the source text, not a proof; each lost loop is listed with its line so the call can be checked.
libc++ 18 spells the hardening mode into the ABI tag of its inline functions ([abi:ne180100] under NONE, [abi:fe180100] under FAST); FAST names are mapped to the NONE spelling before matching.

A loop vectorized in NONE whose function is not inlined the same way in FAST can move: it is counted as moved (not lost) when the same source location gains a vectorized copy in another function of the same file.
